metadata.title: Similarity Estimation Techniques from Rounding Algorithms
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: Registry expected Indyk-Motwani 1998 'Approximate nearest neighbors: towards removing the curse of dimensionality' (STOC'98). The PDF at this BID is in fact Charikar 2002 'Similarity Estimation Techniques from Rounding Algorithms' (STOC'02), which CITES the Indyk-Motwani 1998 paper as reference [31] and reproves their main ANN result in Section 5. Extraction is for the Charikar 2002 paper actually present in the file.

nodes.name: Locality Sensitive Hashing Scheme
nodes.statement: A distribution on a family $\mathcal{F}$ of hash functions on a collection of objects such that for any two objects $x, y$, $\Pr_{h \in \mathcal{F}}[h(x) = h(y)] = \mathrm{sim}(x, y)$, where $\mathrm{sim}(x, y) \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.statement_clean: An LSH family is a hash distribution whose collision probability equals the similarity sim(x,y).

nodes.name: Indyk-Motwani LSH (variant definition)
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{F}$ is $(r_1, r_2, p_1, p_2)$-sensitive for similarity $\mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ if $\Pr_{h \in \mathcal{F}}[h(x) = h(y)] \geq p_1$ when $\mathrm{sim}(x, y) \geq r_1$ and $\Pr_{h \in \mathcal{F}}[h(x) = h(y)] \leq p_2$ when $\mathrm{sim}(x, y) \leq r_2$, with $r_1 > r_2$ and $p_1 > p_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Indyk-Motwani's parameter-based LSH definition with thresholds (r1,r2,p1,p2).

nodes.name: Jaccard Set Similarity
nodes.statement: For sets $A, B \subseteq U$, $\mathrm{sim}(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Jaccard coefficient: ratio of intersection size to union size.

nodes.name: Dice Coefficient
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Dice}}(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{\frac{1}{2}(|A| + |B|)}$.

nodes.name: Overlap Coefficient
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Ovl}}(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{\min(|A|, |B|)}$.

nodes.name: Earth Mover Distance (EMD)
nodes.statement: Given points $L = \{l_1, \ldots, l_n\}$ with metric $d$ and two distributions $P, Q$ on $L$, $\mathrm{EMD}(P, Q)$ is the optimal value of the minimum-cost transportation $\min \sum_{i,j} f_{i,j} d(i,j)$ subject to $\sum_j f_{i,j} = p_i$, $\sum_i f_{i,j} = q_j$, $f_{i,j} \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: EMD is the min-cost transportation between two distributions on a metric space.

nodes.name: Min-wise Independent Permutations Hash
nodes.statement: For a random permutation $\pi$ of universe $U$ and subset $A \subseteq U$, $h_\pi(A) = \min\{\pi(A)\}$. Then $\Pr_\pi[h_\pi(A) = h_\pi(B)] = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Min-wise hashing: take the minimum element under a random permutation; collision probability equals Jaccard.

nodes.name: Random Hyperplane Hash $h_{\vec r}$
nodes.statement: Choose $\vec r$ from the $d$-dimensional Gaussian distribution. Define $h_{\vec r}(\vec u) = 1$ if $\vec r \cdot \vec u \geq 0$ and $h_{\vec r}(\vec u) = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.statement_clean: Hash a vector by the sign of its inner product with a random Gaussian vector.

nodes.name: Classification with Pairwise Relationships
nodes.statement: Given objects $V$, labels $L = \{l_1, \ldots, l_n\}$, assignment cost $c(u, l)$ and edges $e=(u,v)$ with weights $w_e$, find labeling $h: V \to L$ minimizing $\sum_{u \in V} c(v, h(v)) + \sum_{e=(u,v) \in E} w_e\, d(h(u), h(v))$.

nodes.name: Continuous-Set Representation $S(P)$ of a Distribution
nodes.statement: For a distribution $P = (p_1, \ldots, p_n)$, define $S(P) = \bigcup_i [i-1, i] \times [0, p_i] \subset \mathbb{R}^2$. Universe elements are points $[i-1,i] \times \alpha$, with $[i-1,i] \times \alpha \in S(P)$ iff $\alpha \leq p_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: View a distribution as a union of rectangles in R^2; intersection/union areas play the role of set intersection/union.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (Triangle inequality necessary)
nodes.statement: For any similarity function $\mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ that admits an LSH family, the distance $1 - \mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ satisfies the triangle inequality.
assumptions: $\mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ admits an LSH family in the sense of (1)

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (Binarization)
nodes.statement: Given an LSH family $\mathcal{F}$ for similarity $\mathrm{sim}(x,y)$, one can obtain an LSH family $\mathcal{F}'$ that maps objects to $\{0,1\}$ and corresponds to the similarity $\frac{1 + \mathrm{sim}(x,y)}{2}$.
conclusions: There exists a $\{0,1\}$-valued LSH family for $\frac{1+\mathrm{sim}(x,y)}{2}$

nodes.name: Lemma 3 (Isometric Hamming Embedding)
nodes.statement: For any similarity $\mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ that admits an LSH family, the distance $1 - \mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ is isometrically embeddable in the Hamming cube.
conclusions: $1 - \mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ embeds isometrically into the Hamming cube

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (LSH for EMD via Kleinberg-Tardos rounding)
nodes.statement: The Kleinberg-Tardos rounding scheme yields a locality sensitive hashing scheme such that $\mathrm{EMD}(P, Q) \leq \mathbb{E}[d(h(P), h(Q))] \leq O(\log n \log \log n)\, \mathrm{EMD}(P, Q)$.
assumptions: $P, Q$ are distributions on a finite metric $L = \{l_1, \ldots, l_n\}$
$h$ is the hash function induced by Kleinberg-Tardos rounding applied to the LP fractional solution

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Indyk-Motwani $\epsilon$-PLEB on Hamming space)
nodes.statement: For any $\epsilon > 0$, there exists an algorithm for $\epsilon$-PLEB in $H^d$ using $O(dn + n^{1 + 1/(1+\epsilon)})$ space and $O(n^{1/(1+\epsilon)})$ hash function evaluations per query.
assumptions: Data are $n$ points in the $d$-dimensional Hamming cube $H^d$

nodes.name: Random Hyperplane Collision Probability
nodes.statement: For vectors $\vec u, \vec v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $h_{\vec r}$ defined by a Gaussian random vector $\vec r$, $\Pr[h_{\vec r}(\vec u) = h_{\vec r}(\vec v)] = 1 - \frac{\theta(\vec u, \vec v)}{\pi}$, where $\theta(\vec u, \vec v)$ is the angle between $\vec u$ and $\vec v$.
conclusions: $\Pr[h_{\vec r}(\vec u) = h_{\vec r}(\vec v)] = 1 - \theta(\vec u, \vec v)/\pi$

nodes.name: No LSH for Dice and Overlap Coefficients
nodes.statement: The Dice coefficient $\mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Dice}}$ and the Overlap coefficient $\mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Ovl}}$ do not admit any locality sensitive hash function family, since the corresponding distances $1 - \mathrm{sim}$ violate the triangle inequality on $A=\{a\}, B=\{b\}, C=\{a,b\}$.
conclusions: Hence neither admits an LSH family

nodes.name: Weighted-Set LSH from Kleinberg-Tardos (uniform metric)
nodes.statement: The Kleinberg-Tardos rounding scheme on the uniform metric induces a hash $h$ on distributions $P, Q$ with $\Pr[h(P) = h(Q)] \geq \frac{\sum_i \min(p_i, q_i)}{\sum_i \max(p_i, q_i)}$, generalizing min-wise independent permutations to non-negative real weights.
assumptions: $h$ is derived from the Kleinberg-Tardos rounding for the uniform metric
conclusions: Specializes to min-wise independent permutations when weights are $\{0,1\}$

nodes.name: Set Similarity from Random Hyperplane Hash
nodes.statement: Representing sets by their characteristic vectors, the random hyperplane hash gives $\Pr[h(A) = h(B)] = 1 - \theta/\pi$, where $\theta = \cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{|A \cap B|}{\sqrt{|A| \cdot |B|}}\right)$.
assumptions: Sets $A, B$ are represented by their $\{0,1\}$ characteristic vectors

nodes.name: Weighted-Set Collision Probability (eq. 8)
nodes.statement: $\Pr[h(P) = h(Q)] = \frac{|S(P) \cap S(Q)|}{|S(P) \cup S(Q)|} = \frac{\sum_i \min(p_i, q_i)}{\sum_i \max(p_i, q_i)}$.

nodes.name: Hash composition collision (Lemma 2 identity)
nodes.statement: $\Pr_{h \in \mathcal{F}, b \in \mathcal{B}}[b(h(x)) = b(h(y))] = \frac{1 + \mathrm{sim}(x,y)}{2}$.

nodes.name: Random Hyperplane LSH for Vectors
nodes.statement: Construct an LSH family for vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ by sampling random Gaussian vectors and outputting the sign bit of the inner product, yielding collision probability $1 - \theta(\vec u, \vec v)/\pi$.
output: A $t$-bit hash vector for each input vector such that estimated angle $\theta(\vec u,\vec v) = \pi \cdot \mathrm{HammingDist}(h(\vec u), h(\vec v))/t$
nodes.pseudocode: For $j = 1, \ldots, t$: sample $\vec r_j$ from $d$-dim Gaussian. For each input vector $\vec u$: output bit $j$ is $1$ if $\vec r_j \cdot \vec u \geq 0$, else $0$.

nodes.name: EMD Hash via Kleinberg-Tardos Rounding
nodes.statement: Hash family for distributions over a metric space, obtained by solving the Chekuri et al LP for the labeling problem and applying Kleinberg-Tardos rounding (after Bartal HST approximation) to round the fractional label distribution to a single label.
output: A label $h(P) \in L$ with $\Pr[h(P) = l_i] = p_i$ and $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P),h(Q))] \leq O(\log n \log \log n) \mathrm{EMD}(P,Q)$
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Probabilistically embed $L$ into an HST $T'$ via Bartal. 2. Solve the Chekuri-Khanna-Naor-Zosin LP relaxation on $T'$ to obtain a per-object distribution. 3. Apply Kleinberg-Tardos rounding on $T'$ to extract a single label $h(P)$.

nodes.name: Weighted Min-wise Hash (continuous Kleinberg-Tardos rounding)
nodes.statement: Sample an infinite sequence $\{(i_t, \alpha_t)\}$ with $i_t$ uniform in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $\alpha_t$ uniform in $[0,1]$; assign the distribution $P$ the label $i$ corresponding to the first index whose $(i,\alpha)$ lies in $S(P)$.
output: Hash value $h(P) \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$ such that $\Pr[h(P) = h(Q)] \geq \frac{\sum_i \min(p_i,q_i)}{\sum_i \max(p_i,q_i)}$
nodes.pseudocode: Sample $(i_1,\alpha_1), (i_2,\alpha_2), \ldots$ with $i_t$ uniform in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $\alpha_t$ uniform in $[0,1]$. In phase $t$: if $\alpha_t \leq p_{i_t}$ and $P$ has not been assigned a label, set $h(P) = i_t$.

nodes.name: Simple ANN Search via Random Bit Permutations
nodes.statement: Solve approximate nearest neighbor in $H^d$ by maintaining $N = O(n^{1/(1+\epsilon)})$ sorted orderings of the dataset under random bit permutations, and answering queries by binary searches on each ordering followed by bidirectional scans.
nodes.pseudocode: Preprocessing: choose $N = O(n^{1/(1+\epsilon)})$ random permutations $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_N$ of the bits; for each $\sigma$, store the dataset sorted lexicographically by bits permuted by $\sigma$, call this order $O_\sigma$. Query: for each $\sigma$, binary-search $q$ in $O_\sigma$; bidirectionally scan from the located position, advancing the pointer with the longest matching prefix; examine $2N$ vectors total; return the one of smallest Hamming distance to $q$.

nodes.name: Min-wise Independent Permutation Hashing
nodes.statement: For each random permutation $\pi$ of $U$ and set $A \subseteq U$, output $h_\pi(A) = \min\{\pi(A)\}$; estimate Jaccard similarity by counting matching coordinates of hash vectors.

nodes.name: Indyk-Motwani PLEB Construction
nodes.statement: Reduces approximate nearest neighbor on $H^d$ to PLEB (Point Location in Equal Balls), then concatenates several locality sensitive hash function values; achieves the bounds of Theorem 2.
output: Data structure answering $\epsilon$-PLEB queries with $O(n^{1/(1+\epsilon)})$ hash evaluations

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-PLEB (Point Location in Equal Balls)
nodes.statement: Given $n$ points in $H^d$ and a radius $r$, build a data structure that, on query $q$, reports a point at distance $\leq r(1+\epsilon)$ from $q$ if any point is within distance $r$ of $q$.

nodes.name: Approximate Nearest Neighbor in Hamming Space
nodes.statement: Given $n$ points in $H^d$, preprocess them so that for any query $q$ a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate nearest neighbor (a dataset point within $(1+\epsilon)$ times the true minimum Hamming distance) can be reported efficiently.

nodes.name: Estimating Set Similarity from Sketches
nodes.statement: Construct sketches $\mathrm{sk}(x)$ of objects in a collection so that the similarity $\mathrm{sim}(x, y) \in [0,1]$ can be estimated efficiently from $\mathrm{sk}(x), \mathrm{sk}(y)$.

nodes.name: Sketching the Earth Mover Distance
nodes.statement: Construct hash functions on distributions $P, Q$ over a metric space $(L, d)$ such that $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P), h(Q))]$ approximates $\mathrm{EMD}(P, Q)$ up to a small factor.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Show the indicator $\Delta_h(x,y) = [h(x) \neq h(y)]$ satisfies the triangle inequality pointwise; conclude by linearity of expectation that $1 - \mathrm{sim}(x,y) = \mathbb{E}_h[\Delta_h(x,y)]$ also does.

nodes.name: Express $1-\mathrm{sim}$ as collision probability
nodes.statement: From the LSH definition, $1 - \mathrm{sim}(x,y) = \Pr_{h \in \mathcal{F}}[h(x) \neq h(y)] = \mathbb{E}_h[\Delta_h(x,y)]$.

nodes.name: Pointwise triangle inequality on indicator
nodes.statement: Since $\Delta_h \in \{0,1\}$, the only way $\Delta_h(x,y) + \Delta_h(y,z) < \Delta_h(x,z)$ could fail is when both are zero. But then $h(x)=h(y)=h(z)$ so $\Delta_h(x,z)=0$ as well, giving $\Delta_h(x,y) + \Delta_h(y,z) \geq \Delta_h(x,z)$ always.

nodes.name: Take expectations
nodes.statement: By linearity of expectation, $\mathbb{E}_h[\Delta_h(x,y)] + \mathbb{E}_h[\Delta_h(y,z)] \geq \mathbb{E}_h[\Delta_h(x,z)]$, i.e. $1 - \mathrm{sim}$ satisfies the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (binarization)
nodes.statement: Compose any $h \in \mathcal{F}$ with a pairwise independent random map $b: \mathrm{range}(h) \to \{0,1\}$. With probability $\mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ we have $h(x) = h(y)$ giving $b(h(x)) = b(h(y))$; otherwise $\Pr[b(h(x)) = b(h(y))] = 1/2$. Total collision probability is $\mathrm{sim}(x,y) + (1-\mathrm{sim}(x,y))/2 = (1+\mathrm{sim}(x,y))/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3 (isometric Hamming embedding)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 2 to obtain a binary LSH family for $\mathrm{sim}'(x,y) = (1+\mathrm{sim}(x,y))/2$. Concatenating the bits embeds objects into a Hamming cube whose normalized distance equals $1 - \mathrm{sim}'(x,y) = (1 - \mathrm{sim}(x,y))/2$, an isometric embedding of $1 - \mathrm{sim}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (EMD bounds)
nodes.statement: Upper bound follows from property (7) of Kleinberg-Tardos rounding combined with HST approximation. Lower bound: let $y_{i,j} = \Pr[h(P)=l_i, h(Q)=l_j]$; the marginals $\sum_j y_{i,j} = p_i$, $\sum_i y_{i,j} = q_j$ make $\{y_{i,j}\}$ feasible for the EMD LP, so $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P),h(Q))] = \sum_{i,j} y_{i,j} d(i,j) \geq \mathrm{EMD}(P,Q)$.

nodes.name: Upper bound via HST + Kleinberg-Tardos
nodes.statement: Probabilistically approximate the metric on $L$ by an HST $T'$ via Bartal [3,4]; on $T'$ use the Chekuri-Khanna-Naor-Zosin LP and Kleinberg-Tardos rounding which guarantees $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P),h(Q))] \leq O(1) \sum_T \ell_T |P(T) - Q(T)| = O(1)\, \mathrm{EMD}_{T'}(P,Q)$. Since HST distortion is $O(\log n \log \log n)$ in expectation, $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P),h(Q))] \leq O(\log n \log \log n)\, \mathrm{EMD}(P,Q)$.

nodes.name: Lower bound via LP feasibility
nodes.statement: Set $y_{i,j} = \Pr[h(P) = l_i, h(Q) = l_j]$. Property (6) yields $\sum_j y_{i,j} = p_i$ and $\sum_i y_{i,j} = q_j$, so $\{y_{i,j}\}$ is feasible for the EMD LP (2)-(5). Therefore $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P), h(Q))] = \sum_{i,j} y_{i,j} d(i,j) \geq \mathrm{EMD}(P,Q)$.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of ANN correctness (Section 5)
nodes.statement: Set $p_1 = 1 - r/d$, $p_2 = 1 - r(1+\epsilon)/d$, $k = \log_{1/p_2} n$, $\rho = \frac{\ln 1/p_1}{\ln 1/p_2}$. Then $n^\rho = O(n^{1/(1+\epsilon)})$. With constant probability some permutation aligns the true nearest neighbor with $q$ on the first $k$ coordinates, while the number of far points (at distance $> r(1+\epsilon)$) that agree with $q$ on the first $k$ coordinates across all $N$ permutations is at most $2N$.

nodes.name: Set parameters $p_1, p_2, k, \rho$
nodes.statement: Define $p_1 = 1 - r/d$, $p_2 = 1 - r(1+\epsilon)/d$, $k = \log_{1/p_2} n$, $\rho = \frac{\ln 1/p_1}{\ln 1/p_2}$, so that $n^\rho = O(n^{1/(1+\epsilon)})$.

nodes.name: Bound far-point collisions
nodes.statement: For any $q'$ at Hamming distance $\geq r(1+\epsilon)$ from $q$, a random coordinate agrees with $q$ with probability $\leq p_2$, so the first $k$ coordinates agree with probability $\leq p_2^k = 1/n$. Across $N$ permutations the expected count is $\leq N$, and is $\leq 2N$ with probability $> 1/2$.

nodes.name: Probability the true nearest neighbor is found
nodes.statement: For a random permutation $\sigma$, the nearest neighbor agrees in the first $k$ coordinates with probability $p_1^k = n^{-\rho}$. Across $N = n^\rho$ permutations, at least one such agreement occurs with probability $\geq 1 - (1-n^{-\rho})^{n^\rho} > 1/2$.

nodes.name: Conclude correctness
nodes.statement: With constant probability some permutation $\sigma$ has the nearest neighbor among the $2N$ examined vectors, and at most $2N$ far points appear there as well; hence the algorithm reports a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate nearest neighbor with constant probability.

nodes.name: ODP / hierarchical document classification
nodes.statement: Documents assigned a probability distribution over classes in the Open Directory Project (ODP) hierarchy can be sketched via the EMD hashing scheme; since the ODP hierarchy is itself an HST, the approximation factor improves to $O(1)$.

nodes.name: Image similarity via EMD on color/feature distributions
nodes.statement: Images represented as distributions over color/feature points with an underlying metric: EMD measures their similarity, and the proposed hash family yields an $O(\log n \log \log n)$ approximation to EMD usable for retrieval.

nodes.name: Dice / Overlap counterexample on $\{a\}, \{b\}, \{a,b\}$
nodes.statement: For $A = \{a\}, B = \{b\}, C = \{a,b\}$: $\mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Dice}}(A,C) = \mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Dice}}(C,B) = 2/3$, $\mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Dice}}(A,B) = 0$, so $(1-2/3) + (1-2/3) = 2/3 < 1 = 1 - \mathrm{sim}_{\mathrm{Dice}}(A,B)$. Triangle inequality fails; same for Overlap with values $1, 1, 0$.

nodes.name: Two LSH definitions are essentially equivalent
nodes.statement: The Indyk-Motwani $(r_1, r_2, p_1, p_2)$-sensitive definition and Charikar's $\Pr[h(x) = h(y)] = \mathrm{sim}(x,y)$ definition differ formally but capture the same intuition; the name 'locality sensitive hashing' is retained.

nodes.name: Derandomized random hyperplanes
nodes.statement: The random hyperplane hash family for $n$ vectors can be implemented with only $O(\log^2 n)$ random bits using Nisan's pseudorandom generator [35] and constructions of Indyk [30] and Engebretsen-Indyk-O'Donnell [17].

nodes.name: Single data structure for all radii
nodes.statement: Unlike the Indyk-Motwani PLEB-based ANN scheme, the simple permutation-based scheme of Section 5 uses a single data structure that automatically adapts to the unknown nearest-neighbor distance $r$.

nodes.name: Calinescu-Karloff-Rabani 0-extension gives only an upper bound on EMD
nodes.statement: The 0-extension rounding scheme of Calinescu et al [10] yields $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P), h(Q))] \leq O(\log n)\, \mathrm{EMD}(P,Q)$ but does not satisfy the marginal property (6); hence it can produce $\mathbb{E}[d(h(P), h(Q))] = 0$ even when $\mathrm{EMD}(P,Q) > 0$ and provides no lower bound.

nodes.name: Sketching information-theoretic distances (e.g. KL divergence)
nodes.statement: Construct sketching functions to estimate information-theoretic measures of distance between distributions such as the KL divergence; since KL is neither symmetric nor satisfies the triangle inequality, new ideas are required.
